title: NestArc Go overview
answer: NestArc Go is a modular organizer insert for an adult-carried diaper bag; it is not a sleep product, restraint, toy, feeding surface, or medical device.

title: Launch materials
answer: The launch version uses a recycled-PET outer shell, a thermoplastic-polyurethane wipe-clean lining, and removable polypropylene dividers.

title: Size and empty weight
answer: NestArc Go measures 31 × 22 × 12 centimeters and weighs 420 grams when empty.

title: Target launch price
answer: The working direct-to-consumer launch assumption is a $68 MSRP; wholesale pricing and unit economics are not approved in this corpus.

title: Launch timing and colors
answer: The current target is Q2 2027 in slate and moss; this is a roadmap target, not evidence that launch has occurred.

title: Committed launch scope
answer: Committed launch scope is the base insert, six removable dividers, and two labeled wet-item pouches.

title: Synthetic durability results
answer: Three fictional samples completed 20,000 zipper cycles without functional failure; seam failures averaged 18.0 kilograms. These engineering checks are not regulatory certification.

title: Directional caregiver research
answer: In the constructed 50-person exercise, 36 preferred modular dividers and 31 ranked fast retrieval among their top three needs; the sample was not representative and did not test production use.

title: Price objection
answer: Price resistance is material: 21 of 50 fictional participants called $68 too expensive. That directional result does not prove purchase intent or market demand.

title: Wash-instruction conflict
answer: The corpus conflicts by version: a pilot pitch said machine washable, while current launch guidance is spot-clean only because wash durability is unverified. Do not repeat the machine-washable claim for launch.

title: Market-size definitions conflict
answer: The corpus does not support one agreed market size: the $2.4 billion founder estimate includes bags, organizers, and travel accessories, while the $1.1 billion research estimate covers organizers and inserts.

title: Insulated pod is not committed
answer: The insulated bottle pod is a research item, not a launch commitment.

title: No companion app planned
answer: No companion mobile app is planned in the current roadmap.

title: Why modular may matter
answer: The modular layout plausibly addresses faster item retrieval: 36 of 50 fictional caregivers preferred it and 31 prioritized retrieval. This is an interpretation of directional concept research, not proof of demand.

title: Contamination claim unsupported
answer: The corpus does not contain evidence that NestArc Go prevents contamination or keeps baby items sanitary.

title: Infant-sleep claim unsupported
answer: The corpus does not support infant-sleep use or certification; the product brief explicitly defines NestArc Go as an adult-carried organizer, not a sleep product.

title: Specify the product version
answer: Specify whether you mean the pilot pitch or the current launch version before quoting a care instruction; their wash language differs.
